name: Clay-Style 3D
visualIdentity: A supplemental, digital 3D surface treatment: rounded meshes, matte materials, restrained handmade texture, broad lighting, and credible contact shadows. Use weighty forms with slight elasticity; do not imply filmed physical clay or continuously melting shapes.
suitableUses: Explicitly: single-character or product mascot shots. Also fits soft 3D and material-transformation scenes; diorama or narrative worlds when staged consistently. Interactive examples include impact-triggered growth, character response, and bounded parallax when assets support them. These are suitability inferences, not mandatory patterns.
limitations: Omit impact-and-growth when the topic does not support it, growth implies unsupported science, or labels would be obscured. Parallax needs complete layers and preserved contact; orbit needs real 3D or sufficient turntable views, not a single flat image. Keep deformation controlled; XPBD does not itself provide plasticity, fluids, tearing, or clay stop motion.
palette: Suggested only when no task, brand, approved, or existing semantic palette is supplied: background #F2E9DA, foreground #3E4A46, accents #93AD9E and #C7917B. Four discrete colors, limited families; no gradients. Preserve approved colors, role assignments, assets, and material coherence. Foreground on background contrast is 7.675:1; accents are decorative, not body-text backings. Recheck actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Animate weight and slight elasticity, using controlled deformation and keyframes; avoid constant wobble or melting. Interactive patterns may use click/tap plus keyboard activation for drop, contact squash, then outward growth; pointer-based gaze or miniature parallax needs suitable assets and bounded response. Scroll can drive chapters, story states, or a camera orbit only with sufficient geometry. Video must use authored composition time, deterministic seeks, and readable holds; live input is for interactive delivery.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic, audience, narrative, and explicit audio requirements. Avoid competing with speech; synchronize, mix, and inspect picture and sound together. No audio assets are specified.
assetRequirements: Create meshes, materials, lighting, animation, and offline renders in Blender, optionally via its bundled bpy API; Cycles or EEVEE may be selected. Prepare suitable geometry or baked frames for scenes needing 3D depth. Interaction patterns require supporting eye layers/rigs, depth layers, turntable views, or receiving surfaces as applicable. Asset sources are unspecified. Keep simulation deterministic and distinguish simulated appearance from photographed production.
combinations: Alone suits mascot and product shots. With style-079, use a bounded miniature set at consistent scale and matching matte roughness; keep depth of field off key characters. With style-106, use impact-only anticipation, squash, and volume-preserving settle, retaining recognizable silhouettes. Camera orbit is compatible only with real depth; other combinations are not specified.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion engine from style, action, assets, and fidelity; Blender owns visual construction and motion. Optional XPBD needs a verified solver, defined constraints and fixed-step deterministic baking or replay; it is not a style or a universal package. HyperFrames owns composition, timing, sync, validation, and export by default. Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability; record why. Do not mix framework APIs or let the pipeline replace style-specific rendering. Color validation is optional; preserve approved palette. Verify representative frames, decoded video, audio sync, and dimensions.
